//: Input to tools/gen-image.py. Every entry needs `claims` and `omits` before
it can be accepted; check-data.py refuses a made picture without them.
This pack sets allowPhoto true, and it is the only one that does. The rule
it relaxes exists because a photographic plate reads as a RECORD, and for
a subject that predates photography there is no record for it to be
mistaken for. A hillside in October is a present-day thing that
photographs, so photographing it asserts nothing false.
The text rule does NOT relax, and this is the pack it was written for. No
labels, no capsules, no appellation bands, no producer names, no signage.
An invented battle is an illustration; an invented Barolo label is a
forgery, because a label is a legal instrument naming a producer and a
protected origin. Bottles are shot unlabelled, from behind, or cropped.
And nothing here claims a VARIETY. The spike generated a beautiful bunch
of grapes that is not Nebbiolo, and no prompt can fix that: the model
cannot tell Nebbiolo from Barbera from Sangiovese. So the grape pictures
say 'dark grapes' in their claims and say so again in their omits. A
varietal close-up, if this course ever needs one, has to be archive.

langhe-take.style: natural light landscape photograph, muted colour, shallow atmosphere haze

title.en: Fog over the hills in autumn

langhe-take.claims: Rolling hill country under autumn morning fog, of the kind that fills the valleys of north-west Italy in October.
langhe-take.omits: Not a photograph of any identified hill, village or vineyard. No place is being named.
